presentation.label: 1986 DIGITAL REVERB
presentation.summary: All 225 programs of the Alesis Midiverb, Midiverb II and Midifex (63, 99 and 63), run at their original arithmetic.
presentation.overview: Each program is the original unit's, played step for step: the same delay lines, the same 12-bit input, the same 16-bit memory and rounding, at half rate like the original. All 225 programs of the three units, the Midiverb II's chorus and flange programs with their LFOs; the name of each shows while you turn.
highlights: 225 original programs: 63 Midiverb, 99 Midiverb II with its swept choruses and flanges, 63 Midifex
The original's grain: 12-bit input, 16-bit memory, its own rounding
Program and bank names in a message box as you turn
STOP, STOP, STOP cuts the tail; MIX 0 is exact dry
usage: Choose MIDIVRB I/II in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to it and press YES, then press FX2 for the main page.
PROG (A) picks the program in the bank, BANK (D) switches between Midiverb, Midiverb II and Midifex; the message box names each.
LEVL (B) drives the 12-bit input: unity at 32, 64 is +6 dB. MIX (F): 0 dry, 127 wet only.
A new program starts from silence in under a tenth of a second; STOP, STOP, STOP cuts the tail until the track's next trig.

controls.name: PROG
controls.doc: the bank's program; its number and name show in a message box while it turns. 0.1.0's programs keep their places, the ones added in 0.2.0 follow

controls.name: LEVL
controls.doc: input level into the 12-bit converter: unity at 32, 64 is +6 dB

controls.name: BANK
controls.doc: Midiverb, Midiverb II or Midifex programs

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet; 0 is exact dry, 127 wet only

limitations: FX2 only: each instance uses the first 15,870 words of its track's 16K-word FX2 buffer and leaves the last 514 to Sidechain Compressor's key window on T3 and T7.
Patches one stock site of its own (0x4000d568), where each frame's parameters are final; Euclid's patch six bytes before returns into it, so both install together.
Up to 331 executed DSP instructions a sample in the emulator, about 1.05 times stock SPRING REV at its worst (314); the Midiverb II's chorus and flange programs, with their LFOs, are the dearest.

Unlike the original: 22.05 kHz instead of about 23.4 kHz (reverb times and delays about 6 % longer), no model of its analog filters and noise, some long delays up to 4.5 % shorter, and a mono input from the average of left and right. The Midiverb II's chorus and flange LFOs step once every 8 samples, a pace not read from the original, and its three triggered flanges (50, 53, 57) sweep on their own, with no trigger.
On base 0.8.1, the first NO after picking it on FX2 SETUP only closes the memory box: press FX2 for its page instead. Base 0.8.2 fixes it.

With Scale Quantizer or FM Synth installed, the program and bank names do not show and, on base 0.8.1, slow PROG and BANK turns after a pick need an FX2 re-entry: their adapters take the knob store first.

storage.label: DSP program / state
storage.conditions: The USB package: 645 program words on each DSP core it runs on (one copy a core, however many of its tracks run it), 32 words of state per instance, the first 15,870 words of the track's own 16K FX2 buffer in Y memory (the last 514 stay Sidechain Compressor's key window on T3 and T7), and 49,188 bytes of ColdFire code and data holding the 174 programs, their names and the stream; no bss.

processing.label: DSP instruction peak
processing.conditions: perf:audit record: worst 397.1 executed instructions a sample (static floor 395.5), against DARK REV 242.38 and 330.94 for the dearest stock effect. Executed instructions, not chip cycles. On the unit the DSP load of T1-T4 rose 17.8 points with it on T1 FX2.

cpuPrice.conditions: Dev17 bank C: C04 Part 2 (working = saved), picks on the empty C02, the curve on C04 (trigs on steps 1/5/9/13 of T1-T4, T6, T7), transport stopped; twin ed5474c6 of base 0.8.3 (main 80ea1e584); base development twin ed5474c6 of base 0.8.3 (main 80ea1e584), the owner's MKII, OS 1.40C; 3 readings of 8 s a state. Frame interrupt 36.6 % before, 36.6 % installed and used nowhere, 38.9 % on T1 FX2; CPU meter 56.7 % before, 56.7 % at rest, 58.7 % in use.

impact.conditions: One instance at the dearest program in the DSP emulator; on the owner's MKII (development twin 4c7eb79b of base 0.8.1) the frame-interrupt price and the instance curve on Dev17 bank C (picks on the empty C02, readings on C04, trigs on steps 1/5/9/13 of T1-T4, T6 and T7).

cpu.rationale: On the unit the frame interrupt rose 1.1 points with it on T1 FX2 and 0.8 installed and used nowhere; the instance curve read first 0.5, each 0.

dsp.rationale: 397.1 executed instructions a sample worst case, 1.64 times DARK REV (242.38) and 1.20 times the dearest stock effect (330.94); on the unit one instance took about 17.8 points of a DSP core.

memory.rationale: One instance takes its track's whole FX2 buffer (15,870 words), 32 state words, and 645 program words a core; the ColdFire half holds the programs (49,188 bytes).

tests.summary: npm run test:procedure on the owner's MKII (2026-11-25, base 0.8.1 twin): every unit step passed; perf:audit worst 397.1 instructions a sample, the stress run four a core with no clobber; the owner tried it and approved it.
gates: Worst-case cycles under parameter modulation and maximum load
Exact memory region and maximum-instance totals
Owner-reviewed real-hardware evidence with actual coverage and limitations

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every one of the 225 programs streamed by its index at LEVL 127 and MIX 127, unsplit and split at frames 1 and 7, in dsp_host (verify.py --all): the worst block 330.4 executed instructions a sample (Midiverb II #69, an LFO program), with the per-call stream loader and the ring clear; static.py's longest path over each program's units, every conditional add taken: 325.1. On the owner's MKII (27 November 2026) the dearest program, #69, read 613.3 chip cycles a sample on core 1 and 593.0 on core 0 against a NONE baseline, so the package declares 632 hardware cycles (the highest reading, rounded up; the cap is 726).
conditions.parameterModulation: stress.py: three LFOs an instance (LEVL sine, MIX triangle, slot E square) and all twelve slots new every sixteenth; LFOs, locks, scenes and CC reach the engine only as the slot values in its parameter block, which the engine reads each call. Program and bank changes arrive as the ColdFire half's stream; the Midiverb II's chorus and flange programs run their own LFO sweeps inside the engine.
conditions.modeSwitching: A program change fades the wet out, clears the ring and loads the next program from its stream; STOP's tail kill silences the reverb and clears the ring. verify.py checks both bit for bit; stress.py switches programs every sixteenth and holds the tail kill. On the unit device:test switched Parts 12 of 12 with their own effects, and the 120 s soak changed scenes and the crossfader with it installed.
conditions.maxLoad: Four instances a core, eight on both: 4 x 326 = 1,304 executed instructions of the 3,120 a core can spend a sample (stress.py runs four a core on eight tracks). On the unit, admission charges the declared 632 cycles: device:test placed three on each core at once on Dev17 C04 (core peaks 632 and 714 per mille) and refused the fourth on each.
conditions.inputConditions: Full-scale noise bursts (0.98) and silence on the left, tones on the right, in stress.py; verify.py adds bursts of 0.45 and 0.3 with silence before and after. The input passes the original's 12-bit converter (LEVL 127 is about +12 dB), so it clips there as the original did.

memory.conditions: From the header of the USB package d554753c (ABI 8), plus the FX2 buffer it reads: stock's own 16K Y buffer for the slot (Y:$4000 and $8000, and $30000/$34000 on core 0, $38000/$3c000 on core 1, as stock's allocator gives them), of which it uses 15,870 words. No stock block is reused beyond that buffer; no scratch outside its state and buffer (dsp_host's guard counted no stray write).

hardware.summary: On the owner's Octatrack MKII, 27 November 2026, development twin ed5474c6 of base 0.8.3: npm run test:procedure ran on package d554753c (the shipped package, built from source by the isolated build): software checks, compatibility beside 48 modules, the DSP cost model, device:test (self-test; T1 and T5 admitted in about 116 ms; three a core at once; Part switches 12 of 12), the 120 s soak and the put-back passed. The CPU price is 2.3 % of a frame in use and 0 at rest; the instance curve on Dev17 C04 reads first 2, each 2, admitted alone on the empty and the medium pattern with nothing dropped. By hand, 32 of 32 PROG and BANK cases passed: 0.1.0's PROG values keep their programs on all three banks, MV2 PROG 83-102 play the Midiverb II's 50-69, and PROG stops at each bank's last program (63, 102, 63). The owner played it in a trial of this exact package and called the PROG knob great (reported).
limitations: Not run: an emulator rehearsal (the adapted ot_emu runs no DSP with a USB package).
Screens by hand: PROG and BANK message boxes only; the other pages are 0.1.0's captures, unchanged in 0.2.0.
Not done: MAIN and CUE recorded over USB and checked for dropouts.
How it sounds: the owner listened in a RAM trial of d554753c (reported, not item by item); the chorus and flange speeds follow an assumed pace.
Not done: MIDI and recording with it, beside the other modules of a large set on a unit (modules:compat checks the declarations), project save and reload, a Keep and a power cycle.
The procedure ran from a checkout whose only uncommitted changes were the two test-procedure scripts of the step-1 Fix (module source committed as 8bfd1772).

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Load a drum loop on track 1, press FX2, then FUNC + FX2, scroll to MIDIVRB I/II with LEVEL, press YES, then FX2: the page shows PROG, LEVL, BANK and MIX.

Play the pattern and turn A slowly: the message box names each program, from short bright rooms to 20-second halls. Turn D to MV2 for the Midiverb II's programs (its flanges and choruses, 50 to 69 on the original, are the last twenty), or FEX for the Midifex's.
Turn F (MIX) up to hear more of the reverb. Turn it to 0, or press STOP three times, to get the dry loop back.

access.location: Audio track FX2 SETUP: MIDIVRB I/II in the effect chooser.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 to open FX2 SETUP.
Turn LEVEL to MIDIVRB I/II and press YES to assign it.
Press FX2 for the main page: PROG, LEVL, BANK and MIX.
